summary: Hosted canary rollout: traffic split appears stale in eu-west after editing weights (unexpected % distribution)
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports that after editing a Hosted canary rollout from 10% candidate to 25% candidate, observed traffic distribution remained ~10% in eu-west for ~25–35 minutes while us-east reflected the updated weights within ~2–3 minutes.

Impact
- Customer confidence issue: rollout guardrail evaluation is based on per-variant metrics; stale weights in one region makes comparisons misleading.
- Potential risk: customer may continue increasing candidate % based on incomplete signal.
- No confirmed elevated 5xx or latency regression; primary impact is incorrect routing distribution / propagation inconsistency.

Customer report (Northbridge AI)
- Route: hosted chat route "northbridge-prod-chat" (internal route id: rte_8c1f1d2)
- Baseline: llama-3.1-70b-instruct (pinned build 2024-09-26)
- Candidate: llama-3.1-70b-instruct-v2 (pinned build 2024-10-01)
- Edited weights in Console at ~2024-10-03 16:12 UTC from 90/10 to 75/25.
- Their internal analytics (and our Console canary dashboard) showed us-east trending toward 25% candidate quickly, but eu-west continued near 10% candidate.

Expected behavior
- Policy update should propagate to all Hosted regions within SLO (p95 < 5 minutes) and routing should reflect new weights shortly after propagation.

Actual behavior
- eu-west routing appeared to serve stale weights long after edit; eventually self-corrected without customer action.

Environment
- Hosted (prod)
- Regions: us-east, eu-west
- Routing mode: weighted split; stickiness enabled (request-hash) per rollout defaults

Steps to reproduce (as reported)
1) Create Hosted canary rollout (baseline/candidate) on a route.
2) Let it run for ~30 minutes at 10% candidate.
3) Edit rollout weights to 25% candidate in Console.
4) Observe region-level variant distribution: us-east updates quickly; eu-west remains near old distribution for ~25–35 minutes.

Observations / evidence
- Console screenshot (from customer) shows change event at 16:12 UTC and us-east distribution shifting toward ~25% by 16:15 UTC.
- Our internal dashboard "Hosted Rollouts - Variant Split (by region)" indicates eu-west remained ~88–92% baseline / ~8–12% candidate until ~16:45 UTC, then shifted to ~75/25.

Internal investigation notes
Hypothesis A: metrics lag / sampling artifact
- Checked raw request logs (routing decision tag) and confirmed eu-west decisions were actually ~10% candidate during the window (not just delayed metrics).

Hypothesis B: stickiness causing perceived stagnation
- Customer’s traffic is high (~700–900 RPS) and request-hash should still converge to new weights quickly after update if the hashing inputs / ring update is applied.
- us-east converged, eu-west did not, suggesting not a stickiness-only artifact.

Hypothesis C (most likely): policy propagation race / stale policy version acceptance in one region
- Found control-plane propagation logs indicating eu-west briefly received an older policy revision after the update, then did not apply the newer revision due to non-monotonic update handling.

Relevant logs (redacted)
- control-plane policy distributor (eu-west):
  - 2024-10-03T16:12:08Z applied rollout_policy_v2 revision=1842 route=rte_8c1f1d2 weights=baseline:75,candidate:25
  - 2024-10-03T16:12:12Z applied rollout_policy_v2 revision=1841 route=rte_8c1f1d2 weights=baseline:90,candidate:10 (late arrival)
  - 2024-10-03T16:12:13Z INFO "policy update applied" (no monotonic guard in this path)
  - Subsequent update attempts for rev=1842 were retried but rejected as "no-op" by downstream cache layer because payload hash matched local state for rev=1841 (bug: state key was route-only, missing revision)

- data-plane router (eu-west):
  - route=rte_8c1f1d2 effective_revision=1841 split=90/10 sticky=request_hash

Scope
- Observed for 1 customer route; likely possible for any route experiencing closely spaced updates + cross-region propagation jitter.
- Potentially exacerbated by high QPS and frequent edits to rollout steps.

Mitigation taken during incident window
- Advised customer to pause rollout and force candidate=0% if they needed strict control immediately; customer chose to wait as there were no error symptoms.
- Support monitored region distributions and confirmed eu-west corrected by ~16:45 UTC.

Proposed fix
- Enforce monotonic policy revision checks in propagation consumers and/or include revision in cache key so late arrivals cannot overwrite newer state.
- Add retry + version reconciliation logic when regional state diverges.

Resolution
- Engineering implemented monotonic version checks + retries to prevent stale weights being applied when updates arrive out-of-order across regions.
- Fix shipped via redwood/pr_18537 ("Fix: policy propagation race causing stale weights in one region; adds monotonic version checks and retries").
- Verified in staging with forced out-of-order delivery and in prod via canarying the propagation service; no recurrence observed across synthetic edit tests.

Customer communication summary
- Informed customer of root cause (out-of-order propagation leading to stale revision acceptance in eu-west) and confirmed fix deployed.
- Recommended best practice until GA: avoid multiple rapid edits (<60s) to weights; use step schedule or pause between edits when possible.

Follow-ups
- Add automated alert: "regional rollout revision divergence" (per-route) with low-cardinality bucketing.
- Update runbook to include quick check: compare effective revision per region and force reconcile if divergence persists > SLO.
- Add note to GA acceptance criteria: deterministic propagation and monotonic evaluation under high edit frequency.
comments:
2024-10-03 16:18 UTC — Dev Patel (Support)
Acknowledging receipt. Pulling internal canary routing dashboards now. Can you confirm whether you’re viewing region-level split (us-east vs eu-west) and whether stickiness is enabled on the rollout?

2024-10-03 16:23 UTC — Miguel Santos (Customer Success)
Customer confirmed: they’re seeing it per region. Stickiness is enabled (request-hash). They updated weights once (10% -> 25%) via Console, no API calls.

2024-10-03 16:31 UTC — Allison Grant (SRE)
Seeing the same pattern on our internal dashboard: eu-west variant split flatlined around ~10% candidate past 15m. No correlated errors/latency. This looks like routing config staleness, not just metric lag.

2024-10-03 16:40 UTC — Ravi Menon (Routing)
Routing side should reflect new weights immediately after config refresh. If eu-west stayed at 10%, likely the router never got the updated policy (or got reverted). Suggest checking policy distributor logs for out-of-order updates.

2024-10-03 16:52 UTC — Ethan Park (Control Plane)
Found evidence of out-of-order policy revisions in eu-west logs. A late arrival overwrote newer weights. We’re missing a monotonic guard in one consumer path and cache keying is route-only in a layer that should include revision. Looping in Benji to patch + add reconciliation retry.

2024-10-03 17:05 UTC — Dev Patel (Support) — Customer update
We found a likely root cause: an out-of-order policy update in eu-west briefly reverted the weights after your edit. We’re working on a fix to ensure regions only accept monotonic policy revisions. In the meantime, if you need immediate strict control, we can recommend pausing the rollout (candidate 0%) and re-applying weights after a few minutes.

2024-10-04 09:12 UTC — Benji Okafor (Platform)
Patch drafted: enforce revision monotonicity at apply-time; add retries when regional revision diverges from control-plane source of truth. PR going out today (redwood/pr_18537).

2024-10-04 16:28 UTC — Sean Gallagher (SRE)
Ran staging test with injected reorder: without patch, we can reproduce overwrite. With patch, late revision is rejected and state converges. Proceeding with prod canary rollout for propagation service in eu-west first.

2024-10-06 12:41 UTC — Connor O'Brien (Release Engineering)
Prod rollout of propagation fix completed (all regions). Monitoring for 24h; no anomalies. Linked PR: redwood/pr_18537.

2024-10-07 10:03 UTC — Dev Patel (Support) — Customer update
Fix is now deployed to production. Root cause was an out-of-order policy revision in eu-west that could overwrite newer weights; we now enforce monotonic policy revisions and added retries. Please let us know if you observe any split inconsistencies after edits going forward.
resolution_summary: Policy propagation race allowed out-of-order rollout policy revisions to overwrite newer weights in one region; fixed with monotonic revision checks and retries (redwood/pr_18537).
customer_impact_summary: Incorrect/lagging traffic split in eu-west after a rollout weight edit; no confirmed availability degradation, but canary metrics and rollout confidence were impacted.
support_next_steps: Close ticket after customer confirmation; continue monitoring regional revision divergence dashboards for 7 days; feed learnings into Hosted canary GA hardening checklist.
